lead.t: This is minimal change nephrotic syndrome, the commonest cause at this age, and it responds to corticosteroids.

Minimal change nephrotic syndrome (MCNS) (Σ85% of total cases of nephrotic syndrome in children), the glomeruli appear normal or show a minimal increase in mesangial cells and matrix.\nFindings on immunofluorescence microscopy are typically negative
Minimal change nephrotic syndrome (MCNS) may occur after viral infections and allergen challenges.\n

qs.q: Minimal change nephrotic syndrome may occur after which type of infection?
qs.e: MCNS can follow viral infections, reflecting immune involvement. Bacterial, fungal, or parasitic triggers are not described as typical.
